case_title: Surinder Singh v. State (Union Territory of Chandigarh)
previous_criminal_record: No. Court noted a clean record before and after the incident
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated. Defence claimed the accused was on visiting terms with the complainant; the court did not accept this and found no motive or prior connection established
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony; medical (MLR and doctor); forensic/ballistic (CFSL report); recovery of pistol at arrest
aggravating_circumstances: Pistol aimed at the complainant's face after a threat to kill; accused was intoxicated; loaded service pistol used
mitigating_circumstances: No motive or planning proved; no injury caused; long passage of time; clean record before and after; unblemished service record; suspended 1999 and dismissed 2007
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.307 IPC and s.27 Arms Act; rigorous imprisonment of 3 years on each, concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: On 10 July 1999, the victim, an advocate, was sitting in his residential office dictating to his stenographer, with his clerk present. At about 5:30 pm, the accused, a police constable, entered the office in an inebriated condition, claiming to be a beat officer, and asked for water. After drinking the water, the accused pulled out his service pistol, pointed it at the victim and said he would kill ten people that day. The accused asked the victim to stand with raised hands and directed the clerk and stenographer to leave the room. The accused then moved around the table towards the victim and pulled the lever to ready the weapon. The victim lunged and pushed the accused's hand upward, and a bullet struck the ceiling. No one was injured. The accused tried to fire again, but a bullet fell from the pistol. Household members entered and raised an alarm, and the accused fled, leaving a wireless set behind. Police arrived within about 10 to 15 minutes and arrested the accused nearby with the pistol still in hand. A medical examination recorded that the accused was under the influence of alcohol; the accused declined to give urine or blood samples. A forensic report found that the cartridge recovered from the office was fired from the accused's pistol. The stenographer testified that he saw the shot fired through a mesh door, and the clerk testified to the accused's drunken state and to hearing the shot. The victim testified to the sequence of events.
physical_harm: No injury caused to the complainant or any other person
premeditation_planning: Not found. Court said no planning was proved, suggesting the act may have been impulsive
key_evidence_accepted: Ocular evidence of complainant (PW-2) and stenographer (PW-4) that the accused pointed and fired the pistol; medical report and testimony of doctor (PW-7) on intoxication; CFSL ballistic report linking the cartridge to the accused's service pistol; PW-13 evidence on semi-automatic firing mode
witness_credibility: Complainant and PW-4 found categorical and corroborated by medical and ballistic evidence; minor inconsistencies not material; defence version found incredulous; absence of motive did not make the eyewitness account untrustworthy
post_offence_conduct: Fled the office, leaving wireless set and scooter behind; found nearby by police with pistol still in hand; declined to give urine or blood samples
custody_duration: Sentence already undergone: 3 months and 19 days (per court; custody period not separately stated)
bail_history: On bail at the Supreme Court stage; bail bonds discharged. Earlier bail history not stated
trial_duration: offence: 10 July 1999; trial judgment: 25 July 2006; High Court: 19 May 2010; Supreme Court: 26 November 2021
legal_representation: Appellant: Jasbir Singh Malik and Ms. Usha Nandini V (Advocates). State: Manpreet Singh Doabia, Anil Kumar and Sudarshan Singh Rawat (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR lodged; accused arrested; charge sheet filed; trial completed (14 prosecution and 3 defence witnesses)
appeal_history: Trial court (25 July 2006): convicted s.307 IPC and s.27 Arms Act, 3 years RI each, concurrent. High Court (19 May 2010): appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: partly allowed; s.27 conviction set aside; s.307 conviction maintained; sentence reduced to period undergone
prosecution_argument: Concurrent findings of fact limit interference under Art.136; no substantial question of law arises; conviction should stand
defence_argument: (1) absence of motive; (2) absence of intent not imputable from conduct; (3) re-appreciation of evidence, including contradictions and interested witnesses PW-3 to PW-5, with the s.313 version more probable; (4) licensed weapon misuse is not an offence under s.5 Arms Act
legal_principle_applied: s.307 IPC requires intention or knowledge to cause death plus an overt act, injury not necessary; absence of motive not fatal; limited Art.136 interference with concurrent findings; post-1988 s.27 Arms Act requires contravention of s.5 or s.7; proportionality in sentencing
precedent_relied_upon: Relied on: State of M.P. v. Saleem @ Chamaru (2005) 5 SCC 554; Bipin Kumar Mondal v. State of West Bengal (2010) 12 SCC 91. Also cited: Shivaji Genu Mohite (1973) 3 SCC 219. Referred: State of M.P. v. Kashiram (2009) 4 SCC 26; Jage Ram v. State of Haryana (2015) 11 SCC 366; State of M.P. v. Kanha @ Om Prakash (2019) 3 SCC 605
sentencing_rationale: Sentence was disproportionate to the offence given the mitigating factors, so it was reduced to the period already undergone
judicial_mitigating_factors: No motive or planning (possible impulsive act); no injury caused; long passage of time with clean record before and after; unblemished service record apart from this incident; suspension in 1999 and dismissal in 2007 treated as social sanction
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds discharged; s.27 Arms Act conviction and sentence set aside
